papers.title: Scan or Index? large Evidence Coverage, Answer Quality, and Cost in Long-Document RAG
papers.summary: Compares 11 retrieval configurations (lexical, dense, hybrid reranking, and full-document scanning) for long-document RAG on QASPER and textbook questions. Higher evidence coverage does not consistently yield better answers, and reusable dense retrieval is cheaper than paid decision-based methods as query volume grows. The authors argue evidence retention, answer quality, and reuse cost should be treated as complementary selection criteria.

papers.title: Retrieval Augmented Generation Compositionality
papers.summary: Introduces LASAGNA, an open-source framework for controlled RAG evaluation, and tests 450 pipeline configurations across eight benchmarks with corpora from 5K to 200K documents. Strong techniques do not reliably combine (a predicted +47% gain delivered only +17%), retrieval and faithfulness gains stack differently, and the best configuration changes with corpus size. Concludes that new RAG techniques should be evaluated within the full pipeline.
